extracted.subtask_description: A wire-service news dispatch reporting wartime military, political and diplomatic developments for a general newspaper audience, combining official communiqués, battlefield details, casualty figures and government actions. Typically attributes claims to official/military sources and notes uncertainty or censorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute claims to official/military sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece repeatedly attributes assertions to official or military channels (e.g., “the communique revealed,” “military sources said,” “The report indicated,” “the Air Ministry announced”), indicating that factual claims should be sourced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always identify and attribute information to its source (communiqués, military spokesmen, ministries, agencies). Where multiple sources exist, indicate which side made each claim and avoid presenting disputed claims as undisputed fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note censorship or redactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Associated Press Editor's Note—“The censor deleted four words in this dispatch, apparently relating to town being occupied.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When material has been censored or redacted, explicitly note the deletion and, where possible, indicate what aspect of the report is affected so readers understand limits on available information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish Official Communiqués from Combatants
rubrics_metrics.description: The page collects and presents ‘The Day’s War Communiques’ from various commands and nations, printing each side’s version of events (e.g., German High Command, French communiqué, British General Headquarters in France).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include verbatim or clearly attributed summaries of official communiqués from the belligerents; present them side-by-side so readers can see differing claims and emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize key developments in a concise list
rubrics_metrics.description: The article uses a labeled segment: “Developments of the day included:” followed by numbered/ bulleted points summarizing principal events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a short, clearly ordered summary (numbered or bullet list) of the day’s principal developments to give readers a rapid overview before the detailed narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report casualty and damage figures with attribution and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: “France counted her civilian dead in two days of air raids at 147 tonight, reports from various towns swelling the first total of more than 100 persons killed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When quoting casualty or damage totals, attribute the figure to its reporting authority and, if available, include caveats about provisional status, sources, or discrepancies between reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe military movements and geographic specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: The dispatch gives specific locations and maneuvers (e.g., “occupied the town of Arnhem,” “Maastricht,” “attacks extending to around Arnhem, north of the Rhine,” “Fighting along Belgium’s Albert Canal”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise geographic names, front-line features (rivers, canals, forts, airfields) and unit movements to situate readers; where possible, relate these to well-known reference points (cities, rivers) for comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report political and governmental changes with names and posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed reporting of government actions and appointments: e.g., formation of a five-man War Cabinet, listing members and posts (Churchill, Chamberlain, Attlee, Halifax, Greenwood) and ministerial appointments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When covering political developments, list official titles and personnel changes explicitly and, where relevant, include context on why changes were made and immediate political implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include vivid eyewitness/tactical detail and quoted descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The article incorporates vivid action descriptions and quoted pilot accounts (e.g., “dived from 5,000 feet, pulling out at 150 feet after firing 18,000 rounds of machine-gun bullets”), and colorful tactical reporting (bombs amid lines of trucks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where available, include firsthand or quoted tactical descriptions to convey the intensity and texture of combat; attribute such descriptions to the speaker and avoid conflating them with independently verified facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present multiple national perspectives, claims, and denials
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections like “French Deny Bombing Civilians” and repeated presentation of German, British and French communiqués show the article presents rival claims and official denials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the claims and the denials of the parties involved, making clear who asserts what; do not resolve contradictions without corroboration, and present counterclaims rather than endorsing one side’s version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide strategic or analytical context and possible objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The dispatch includes analyst/strategist commentary and framing such as the “Classic battlefield” analysis and “Strategists see four possible objectives,” mapping likely aims of the campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Augment reporting of events with concise strategic analysis (possible objectives, historical comparisons) attributed to military strategists or analysts to help readers interpret significance, and label such analysis clearly as interpretation rather than breaking news.
